questions.question: For an LP solved to optimality, the right-hand-side sensitivity range of constraint $i$ is an interval of values of $b_i$. Which interval is it?
options: Where the current basis stays both feasible and optimal
Where the current optimal plan stays exactly the same
Where constraint $i$ has positive slack at the optimum
Where the LP stays feasible for some basis or other

questions.question: Constraint $i$ of a maximization LP has shadow price $y_i^*$ and RHS sensitivity range $[L,U]$ for $b_i$. How good is the prediction $z^*(b_i^{\mathrm{new}})=z^*(b_i)+y_i^*(b_i^{\mathrm{new}}-b_i)$?
options: Approximate inside $[L,U]$, exact only at $b_i$.
Exact for every $b_i^{\mathrm{new}}$, inside or not.
Exact inside $[L,U]$; outside, it need not hold.
Exact inside $[L,U]$, and an equality outside too.

questions.question: As the right-hand side $b_i$ of a binding constraint in an LP moves towards an endpoint of its RHS sensitivity range, the optimal corner slides along the binding constraints. What happens at the endpoint?
options: Another constraint starts to bind, ending the basis.
The constraint $i$ stops binding and gets positive slack.
The optimal value reaches its largest possible level.
The shadow price of constraint $i$ becomes 0 there.

questions.question: Within its valid range, one kind of parameter change can preserve the optimal solution vector while changing profit, and another can change the solution vector while keeping the same basis and shadow prices. Which change is the second kind?
options: A change in one objective coefficient
A change in two coefficients at once
A change that leaves all data the same
A change in a resource right-hand side

questions.question: A resource constraint of an LP binds at the optimum, and its right-hand side is raised slightly, staying within its RHS sensitivity range. A student claims the production plan stays the same because the shadow price is still valid. Is this right?
options: Yes: a valid shadow price means the plan is unchanged.
Yes: the plan changes only at the range's endpoints.
No: one basis can give new quantities as $b_i$ moves.
No: a new basis is needed for every change of $b_i$.

questions.question: A sensitivity report gives a resource constraint with right-hand side 500, allowable increase 150 and allowable decrease 80. What is its RHS sensitivity range?

A resource with right-hand side 500 has RHS sensitivity range $[420,650]$ and shadow price 3 in a maximization LP. Management proposes raising it to 700. Can the new optimal value be found as $z^*+3\cdot200$?
options: Yes: the shadow price holds for any increase.
Yes: 700 is less than $500+200$.
No: shadow prices only hold for decreases.
No: 700 is beyond the upper end 650.

questions.question: A maximization LP has optimal value 2400. A resource with shadow price 3 has right-hand side 500 and RHS sensitivity range $[420,650]$. The right-hand side is raised to 600. What is the new optimal value?
In an optimal solution of an LP, the constraint 'kg of milk used $\le200$' has slack 30, so 30 kg are unused, and its shadow price is 0. With all other data fixed, what is its RHS sensitivity range?
options: From 170 upwards, with no upper limit
From 200 upwards, with no upper limit
From 0 to 200, any cut being harmless

questions.question: In an optimal solution of an LP, a resource constraint has slack 30 and shadow price 0. The right-hand side is cut by 40 units. Is the effect on the optimal value given by $0\cdot(-40)=0$?
options: Yes: a shadow price of 0 holds for any cut.
Yes: a slack resource never affects the plan.
No: the cut goes 10 units past the unused 30.
No: the effect is $-40$, one per unit cut.

questions.question: For a maximization LP, a resource's right-hand side is raised past the upper end of its RHS sensitivity range. Why can the extra amount beyond the endpoint not be valued at the old shadow price?
options: Beyond the endpoint the LP becomes infeasible.
Another constraint binds there, so the rate changes.
Shadow prices are only defined at the current value.
Beyond the endpoint the shadow price always doubles.

questions.question: When only the right-hand side $b_i$ of an LP changes, the final simplex tableau's objective-row coefficients do not depend on $b_i$. What therefore limits the RHS sensitivity range?
options: Only optimality: reduced costs must keep their signs.
Both conditions, each limiting one end of the range.
Neither, since a right-hand side never changes the basis.
Only feasibility: basic variables must stay nonnegative.

questions.question: A binding resource of a maximization LP has its right-hand side changed within its RHS sensitivity range. Which of these stays the same?
options: The basis and all shadow prices
The values of the basic variables
The optimal objective value
The slack of every constraint

questions.question: For the LP maximize $2x_1+x_2$ subject to $3x_1+x_2\le b_1$ (machine hours, now $b_1=12$), $x_1+x_2\le8$ (labour), $x_1\le3$ (demand), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the optimum is $(2,6)$ with machine hours and labour binding. Over which interval of $b_1$ does this basis stay optimal?

For the LP maximize $2x_1+x_2$ subject to $3x_1+x_2\le b_1$ (machine hours, now $b_1=12$), $x_1+x_2\le8$ (labour), $x_1\le3$ (demand), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the optimum is $(2,6)$ with value 10, and the range of $b_1$ for this basis is $[8,14]$. What is the optimal plan when $b_1=13$?

For the LP maximize $2x_1+x_2$ subject to $3x_1+x_2\le b_1$ (machine hours, now $b_1=12$), $x_1+x_2\le8$ (labour), $x_1\le3$ (demand), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the range of $b_1$ for the optimal basis (machine hours and labour binding) is $[8,14]$. What does the optimal plan look like at the lower endpoint $b_1=8$?
options: $(2,6)$: the plan of $b_1=12$
$(3,5)$: the demand limit binds
$(0,8)$: $x_1$ has just reached 0
No feasible plan exists at $b_1=8$

questions.question: Two resources of an LP have RHS sensitivity ranges $[L_1,U_1]$ and $[L_2,U_2]$, each computed with all other data fixed. Both right-hand sides change at once, each staying inside its own range. Is the optimal value then certain to change by $y_1^*\Delta_1+y_2^*\Delta_2$?
options: No: each range holds the other data fixed.
Yes: each change is inside its own range.
Yes: shadow prices of different resources add up.
No: two changes at once always change the basis.

questions.question: In an LP whose optimal basic variables are all positive, the right-hand side of resource $i$ is changed within its RHS sensitivity range, and the optimal plan turns out to be exactly the same as before. What must be true of resource $i$?
options: It binds, and its shadow price is positive.
It binds, and its shadow price is 0.
It has slack, and its shadow price is 0.
Nothing, as plans never change inside a range.

questions.question: For the LP maximize $2x_1+x_2$ subject to $3x_1+x_2\le b_1$ (machine hours, now $b_1=12$), $x_1+x_2\le8$ (labour), $x_1\le3$ (demand), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the optimum is $(2,6)$ with value 10; machine hours have shadow price 0.5 and range $[8,14]$, labour has shadow price 0.5 and range $[6,12]$. If $b_1$ becomes 14 and labour becomes 7 at the same time, what is the optimal value?

For the LP maximize $2x_1+x_2$ subject to $3x_1+x_2\le b_1$ (machine hours, now $b_1=12$), $x_1+x_2\le8$ (labour), $x_1\le3$ (demand), $x_1,x_2\ge0$, the optimum is $(2,6)$ with value 10, and machine hours have shadow price 0.5 with range $[8,14]$. A supplier offers 6 extra machine hours for 0.4 each, as one package. Does the package pay?
options: No: only 2 hours add value, worth 1 in total.
Yes: $6\cdot0.5=3$ exceeds the cost $2.4$.
Yes: each hour is worth 0.5 and costs 0.4.
No: hours above the range make the LP infeasible.
